stories.title: Kiev should beg Moscow for peace to save Ukraine — former Zelensky spokesperson
stories.summary: Yulia Mendel said this is now a matter of the country’s "survival"
article_sentences: Ukraine should beg Russia for peace to save the country, former Vladimir Zelensky spokeswoman Yulia Mendel said.
She pointed to the current situation in Ukraine, noting the closure of Black Sea ports and soaring fuel prices.
"Ukraine needs to beg for peace," Mendel wrote on her X page.
In her view, this is now a matter of the country’s "survival." "The longer this goes on, the more the country collapses under the weight of Zelensky's stubbornness," Mendel stressed.
Zelensky’s former press secretary previously spoke out about ending the conflict following an incident involving the forced mobilization of a Kiev resident with his dog.

stories.title: Cuba to withstand US pressure — Fidel Castro’s grandson
stories.summary: Fidel Antonio Castro Smirnov said that Cuba’s experience has demonstrated the importance of "international solidarity, diversification of ties, and the ability of countries to support each other"
article_sentences: Cuba has withstood pressure from the United States for decades and will be able to cope with it today, Fidel Antonio Castro Smirnov, Cuban Revolution leader Fidel Castro’s grandson and professor at the Havana University, told TASS.
"It becomes increasingly difficult to isolate a state when it has reliable partners, alternative markets, financial mechanisms, research ties, and own technological capabilities.

For decades, Cuba has been maintaining international ties, developing cooperation with partners, despite the external pressure and will be able to withstand the US pressure today too," he said, announcing the 2nd World Public Assembly in Moscow on September 18 and 19 that will be titled "A New World: Values That Unite."

According to Castro Smirnov, Cuba’s experience has demonstrated the importance of "international solidarity, diversification of ties, and the ability of countries to support each other for successful sovereign development."
"This is why the World Public Assembly is so important today.

It is a venue where representatives from different countries and cultures can directly discuss new principles of international cooperation and work together to outline new vectors for global development for decades to come," he stressed.

According to the Assembly’s organizers, taking part in expert discussions will be Yemen’s former President Ali Nasir Muhammad, Egypt’s former Foreign Minister Mohamed El-Orabi, former Secretary General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Rashid Alimov, US historian and nuclear expert Peter Kuznick, and other international experts, scientists, diplomat, and public activists.
The first World Public Assembly was held in September 2025 and involved more than 5,000 delegates from 153 world nations.
